question: Does an exact source-bound right-side crop of Xing NLC-CBM1408 original juan45 second limit table PDF p66 recover the L35 ordinal missed by 13WF's left-side crop, and does this change numeric or lineage decisions?

source.accession: NLC892-CBM1408-371933 / 邢雲路《古今律曆考》七十二卷 第14冊 / 同一已登记纸本扫描来源

replay.method: Original source PDF p66 6x render, right-side ONLY (no OCR), source crop manually viewed; rendered pixels do not add original optical detail

direct_visual_observations.observation: The right-side source-PDF crop directly displays printed 三十五限, between neighbouring 三十四限 and 三十六限, correcting 13WF's left crop omission.

The same printed L35 vertical band visibly contains the 疾度 / 遲度 labels and adjacent printed numeric fragments; individual multi-place target values and last digits were not fully adjudicated or compared across printings.

limitations: Sixfold rasterization improves inspectability only; native source JPEG2000 image remains 1738×1481 and no new optical information has been acquired.
Xing original table-B L35 visible row and column do not decide whether the Xu-An L132 final glyph prints 二 or 三.
Same CBM1408 source file as 13WF; no independent physical-copy, print-plate, stemma or numerically identical G893 field is established.
No OCR, no original image bytes or page crops added to the public repository.
next_action: Prioritize a genuinely independent, legible original Xu-An second-table L132 printed terminal 二/三 and the source-specific 疾捷法 coefficient, 少/微 radix/carry, and G893 exact same-field historical crosscheck. Do not repeat now-closed p66 L35 ordinal crop.

edges_rejected_or_unproved: Right-side p66 re-crop and earlier left crop represent the SAME Xing CBM1408 original scan, not independent copies or plate votes.
unresolved_lineage_questions: Can a physically independent Xu-An original j45 table-B L132 target folio resolve the damaged digit and printing-plate identity?

workflow_cleanup: One-shot research workflow removed together with publication of this evidence; successful run and logs remain accessible.
